title: Design System: Live Luxe Partner Portal

gold-ink.displayName: Gold Ink (gold as text on light surfaces, 5.2:1 on cream)

display.purpose: KPI figures and the one hero number on a page (a quote total).

headline.purpose: Page title, one per page, under a gold eyebrow.

title.purpose: Panel headings and the property name on a stay card.

body.purpose: All running text, controls and table cells.

label.purpose: Field labels, pills, table column heads.

eyebrow.purpose: Uppercase gold line above a headline; Gold Ink on light, Gold Bright on navy.

mono.purpose: Booking references, claim/PO numbers, door codes, IPs.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Hovered card list item, date popover.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Field focus halo (fields); buttons use a 2px ring with 2px offset.

motion.name: ease-ios
motion.purpose: The one curve for every transition.

motion.name: duration-control
motion.purpose: Hover, focus and press on controls.

motion.name: duration-theme
motion.purpose: Cross-fade when switching theme, applied only while switching.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Active state on buttons; none on link buttons.

narrative.overview:
A well-staffed front desk in a serviced apartment building. The partner (an insurance claims officer with a family in a motel tonight) walks up, says what they need, and it is handled. The surface is cream paper; the writing is navy ink; there is exactly one gold detail in view, and it marks the thing to do next. Nothing shouts, nothing is decorative for its own sake, and every figure lines up because the page may be printed into a claim file an hour later.

The system is an Operate-mode product UI wearing a premium operator's identity. Density is moderate: one subject per panel, generous panel padding (1.25rem), 44 px controls, tables that become card lists on a phone. The craft is borrowed from Apple's Human Interface Guidelines (surface layering, modest radii, a single press curve, restraint in shadow) so the portal reads as a native tool, not a web template. Brand lives in precise details: the serif heading, the gold eyebrow and underline, the navy ops header, the cream partner header.

Two themes exist. Components never name a raw colour; they name a role (card, border, strong, muted-foreground) and the role is remapped for dark mode and for print. The ops console header stays navy in every theme so staff always know which side of the desk they are on.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper, navy ink, one gold detail per screen.
Serif display (Newsreader) over a humanist sans (DM Sans); mono (Geist Mono) only for references and codes.
Flat, hairline-bordered white panels on cream; shadow reserved for things that lift.
44 px touch floor on every control; tabular figures everywhere numbers appear.
Status is always a labelled pill, never a bare colour.
Partner chrome cream, Live Luxe operations chrome navy, in both light and dark themes.

rules.name: The Gold Is Not Ink Rule
rules.body: Antique Gold is a fill, border and ring colour. As text on any light surface it fails contrast, so text that must be gold uses Gold Ink. On navy, Antique Gold is the text colour (7.3:1).

rules.name: The One Gold Action Rule
rules.body: At most one gold-filled control per screen: the thing the visitor came to do (Submit request, Accept the proposal, Secure with a card hold). Everything else is navy, outline or ghost.

rules.name: The Role Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Components reference roles (card, border, strong, muted-foreground, accent), never a brand hex. Dark mode and print are 25-line remaps, not rewrites.

rules.name: The Navy Side Rule
rules.body: The operations header is Harbour Navy in both themes; the partner header is cream in light and night-surface in dark. The two sides of the desk must never look the same.

rules.name: The Serif Is a Heading Rule
rules.body: Newsreader appears on h1, h2, h3, the wordmark, KPI figures and the property name. It never sets body copy, labels, buttons or table cells.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Tables, definition lists, times and anything with .tabular-nums use tabular figures so money and dates align without opting in per cell.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A panel never carries a shadow at rest. If a surface needs to feel lifted, it is because it is above the page (header, popover, dialog), not because it is important.

dos: Do put one gold-filled action on a screen and make it the thing the visitor came for (The One Gold Action Rule).
Do set gold text in Gold Ink (#866206) on light surfaces and Antique Gold on navy; never Antique Gold on cream.
Do keep every control 2.75rem tall and every tap target 44 px, including table-row buttons on phones.
Do label every status with words inside its pill; colour is reinforcement, never the message.
Do use roles (card, border, strong, accent) rather than brand hexes so dark mode and print stay correct.
Do show money as AUD $1,837.00 with tabular figures, and timestamps in Melbourne time with the zone shown.
Do keep the ops header navy and the partner header cream in both themes.
Do make request detail pages print as a clean A4 document: no chrome, no controls, panels unbroken.
donts: Don't add shadows to panels at rest, or use neutral-black shadows; lift only header, popovers and dialogs with navy-tinted shadow.
Don't set body copy, labels, buttons or table cells in the serif; Newsreader is for headings, the wordmark and hero figures.
Don't use gradients, glass panels, hero imagery or marketing patterns inside the operational screens.
Don't introduce a second accent; status colours are the only colours beyond navy, gold and cream.
Don't exceed 0.875rem radius on panels or go below 0.5rem on controls; no square corners, no capsule buttons.
Don't uppercase anything except eyebrows and table column heads.
Don't reach for a card inside a card; subdivide a panel with hairline sections and a GroupLabel.
